title: actl tickets approve lets exactly the change a hard_block page listed merge
objective: The main session can record the user's approval of a hard_block stop with `actl tickets approve N --page P --reason R`, after which the ticket is re-queued and its issuer merges it only while its own change still has the approved hits and fingerprint, stopping it again with a fresh page when the change differs.
outline: devloop/tickets.py: an 'approve' subparser (positional id, --page required, --reason required, --by default 'user', the default ticket_creator's decide uses) after 'login-ok', and cmd_approve(pool, args) next to cmd_login_ok: one pool.update whose change raises osx.OSFailure (main prints it as 'tickets: <why>', exit 2) unless the id is a ticket id, the ticket exists, it is 'stuck' with stuck.reason 'hard_block' and a stuck.hard_block dict, the page is in tx.data.inbox with ref == the id and a 'hard_block' dict whose fingerprint equals the ticket's stuck.hard_block fingerprint, and the reason is not blank. Then in the same change: t['approval'] = {by, at: osx.now(), reason, page, fingerprint, paths, lines} copied from stuck.hard_block; event(t, 'hard_block approved', by=..., reason=..., page=..., fingerprint=...); state ready, round 0, stuck None, run None; leave_group(tx, t); tx.put_ticket(t); ack_in(tx, page, by); close_pages(tx, id, 'tickets approve'). All checks inside the change (the pool re-applies a change after a rejected push). devloop/ticket_issuer.py: module-level approval_pending(t) next to brief_revised; in go(), right after claim(): self.worker_ok = approval_pending(t). hard_block(self, g, t=None): after building the detail (ticket before this one), when there are hits and t carries an 'approval' dict whose paths, lines and fingerprint all equal the detail's, write the event 'hard_block approval applied' (by, approved_at, fingerprint) with self.save and return; otherwise, when an approval exists, put the 'no longer matches' line of B4 as the text's second line, then raise as before (the approval stays on the ticket). _round calls self.hard_block(g, t) with the ticket it re-reads right before (the line after 'the worker may have had the ticket revised'). Every ticket writer mutates the record it loaded (checked by grep of put_ticket), so 'approval' survives them. Docs per B9.

B4 builds F1 as written (assert first that inspect.signature(Issuer.hard_block) has a parameter named t, so the case fails by assertion on today's code). B5 and B6 run the real controller and scripts as written (the stop, the ready-like state, the move, the surviving worktree and the replayed commit were measured by the opener on main 4797416 with `tickets ready` in place of approve). Remove every DEVLOOP_* variable from self.env in setUp. Expected values come from this ticket's text. Implementer: B7 and B8 with its own tests in tests_devloop/test_issuer.py between class IssuerLock and class RedCheck, and B9; do not add test_approve to board/config.json's map (the map only serves manual selection; the suite discovers the file).
notes: Source: D-103 (user's words '1 選a': the approval is bound to the ticket's change at that moment, who and when are recorded, and a later change needs approval again); the request binds it to the fingerprint of the own change that the ticket before this one records, so a D-098 replay keeps it valid. Measured on main 4797416 with the loop harness (with `tickets ready` where approve will be): after the hard_block stop of a lone ticket, `tickets ready 1` leaves it ready with group null and `dag_edit.py move 1 --to new` places it; on the next run the worker started again (counter 2) and stopped at the same place; <worktrees>/t1 survives the stop on t/1 and a commit made there was replayed by the next run ('rebased', replayed 2). Design choices: (1) approve re-queues with the same transition as `tickets ready N` and writes only its own event, and the first round after it starts no worker: the request asks the issuer to run its merge step again, and a new worker run costs an agent run and could change the approved change; a later round, a revision or a ready ends the skip. (2) CLI only, like D-096: the board gets no approve button (board.ACTIONS stays as it is). (3) the approval stays on the ticket after a mismatch so the fresh page can say it no longer matches; a new approve replaces it. (4) --by defaults to 'user' like ticket_creator's decide. (5) the approval is state written by tickets.py, like 'stuck', not ticket content. Two copies of the hit list exist on purpose: the page row (what was shown) and stuck.hard_block (the current stop); approve requires their fingerprints to be equal, then t['approval'] is the only copy the issuer reads (stuck is cleared by the ready transition). #147, stopped before hit lists existed, has none on its page: approve refuses it, and the main session readies it once so it stops again with a hit list. Group new-g1 (see the ticket before). Merge stop for this ticket's own branch: no added line (code, tests, comments, docs, fixtures) may contain any of this project's four hard_block patterns, i.e. the text os.kill, killpg, pkill, or the word kill followed by a space and a dash. Fixtures use invented patterns (FORBIDDEN_MARK, zz_forbidden, as the existing tests do) instead of the real ones. Do not edit docs/DECISIONS.md or docs/VISION.md of this repository (a fixture may create a docs/DECISIONS.md inside its throwaway test project; that is not this repository's file).

request:
Add a user approval path for tickets stopped by hard_block (decision D-103 in docs/DECISIONS.md; user's words "1 選a").

Problem (confirmed in code): `TicketIssuer.hard_block()` in devloop/ticket_issuer.py raises Stuck("hard_block") when the
ticket's own change touches a hard_block path or adds a line matching a hard_block pattern. The stuck decision page only
offers revise / cancel / retry. A ticket whose job necessarily matches a pattern (e.g. #147, which must send signals to
the process group it started) can never pass: retry stops at the same place, and there is no way to record the user's
approval. The rule "hard_block tickets stop before merge for the user's ruling" has no ruling step.

Wanted:
1. The hard_block stuck page lists exactly what matched: each hit path, and each added line that matched a pattern
   (file and line text), so the user can judge it from the page.
2. A new answer on that page: approve. CLI, main session only (not the board, like D-096): e.g.
   `actl tickets approve N --page P --reason "..."`. It records in the ticket's state who approved, when, the reason,
   and a fingerprint of the change that was shown (computed from the ticket's own change, the same lines/paths
   hard_block inspects, so a replay of the same commits onto a newer target head under D-098 keeps the approval valid).
   Then the ticket is re-queued so the issuer runs its merge step again.
3. On the next hard_block check, if the current hits and the fingerprint of the ticket's own change equal the
   approved fingerprint, the check passes and the merge goes on; the approval is written to the ticket history.
   If the change differs in any way (new lines, new paths, different content), the approval does not apply and the
   ticket stops again with a fresh page that says the earlier approval no longer matches.
4. Approve is offered only on hard_block stuck pages; other stuck reasons keep their current answers.
5. devloop/README.md (the stuck page answers) and CLAUDE.md's answer list mention approve.

The code of this ticket itself must not add lines matching A's hard_block patterns (`os\.kill`, `killpg`, `pkill`,
`kill -`) and must not edit docs/DECISIONS.md or docs/VISION.md. In tests, write such strings so the pattern does
not match the source line (e.g. build them by concatenation).

Acceptance: a ticket stopped by hard_block, approved, then retried with the same change passes the check and merges;
the same ticket with one extra matching line after approval stops again; approve on a non-hard_block page is refused;
the page shows the matched lines.

vision: a hard_block stop becomes a real user ruling: the user sees what matched and approves that exact change, and
a later change needs approval again.
removes: nothing.
